Digital India.question: What is Online infrastructure initiative in India?
Digital India.fact: Digital India is a flagship initiative of the Government of India that aims to transform the country into a "digitally empowered society and knowledge economy" by expanding digital infrastructure, promoting e‑governance, and enabling digital delivery of public services.  The programme was launched on 1 July 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during Digital India Week and is coordinated primarily by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) with participation from multiple ministries and state governments.  Digital India is commonly framed around three key vision areas: providing digital infrastructure as a utility to every citizen, delivering governance and services on demand, and digitally empowering citizens through universal access to digital resources and platforms.  The programme integrates and re‑orients a wide range of earlier information and communication technology (ICT) and e‑governance projects into an umbrella initiative, including BharatNet, DigiLocker, UPI, UMANG, and sector‑specific platforms in health, education, agriculture, and social protection

Digital India.fact: The Digital India programme was formally announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and launched on 1 July 2015 during Digital India Week, with the stated objective of bringing together multiple ICT initiatives under a single umbrella.  The government characterised it as a multi‑departmental, multi‑phase programme to be implemented in partnership with central ministries, state governments, industry, and civil society.  Over time, Digital India has evolved from primarily an e‑governance initiative to a broader digital public infrastructure (DPI) ecosystem built around digital identity, real‑time payments, electronic document storage, and consent‑based data sharing.  In later years, the government launched India Stack Global to present selected Indian digital platforms as exportable DPI models and to promote cooperation with other countries.  At the grassroots level, Digital India initiatives are implemented by local entrepreneurs and CSC operators. Digital India.fact: The rise of fintech and digital commerce has been closely linked to Digital India. Government‑backed platforms such as Government e‑Marketplace (GeM) and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) seek to digitise procurement and retail, including participation by micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
